question: Given assigned crowd sizes and pre-task map information, can a fixed LLM improve left/right exit-choice probability relative to simple rules and calibrated Logit?
exclude: 58 equal-crowd records with biased map codes 1/2, whose absolute direction cannot be resolved from README alone; retained in original case table.
validation: Leave out a mirror family defined by sorted(left_count,right_count) and original knowledge code. Mirrors always excluded together. Balanced cases have one self-mirror condition. No random record split.
data_visibility: Whole-source structural fields and counts were inspected. This is exploratory grouped validation, not unseen external confirmation.
input: map states equal or nearer final exit
fixed common geometry and task instruction
counts_semantics: Assigned experimental scene counts, not measured queue length at an exact decision timestamp.
common_geometry: 20m square room; avatar equidistant from two 1.5m-wide room doors; map, when provided, describes onward relative proximity to final exit. No smoke observation or staff instruction treatment.
training_weights: Equal total weight per condition, equal per participant record within condition.
frequency_prior: One pseudo-participant at p_left=0.5 per fit
rule_calibration: Train-fold agreement with recommendation; Laplace(1,1). Tied/unknown recommendations return p_left=0.5.
learning_disclosure: Logit and rule calibration use training-family outcomes. LLM receives only training-family base frequency plus current scene, no few-shot outcomes. Same scene information does not mean identical learning procedure.
no_tuning: No alternate prompts, larger models, regularization search or outcome-driven map decoding in this run.
scope: Human choices in virtual scene among valid completed uploads. No dynamic replanning, guidance causality or fire-control efficacy claim.
